concepts.why: Close reading of name against passages: the name is a command to acquire; Job 28:15-18 says wisdom cannot be bought with gold or silver, i.e. it is the question of where wisdom is found, not an instruction to get it. Move it to concept 6, where it belongs beside Job 28:12-14 and 20-23. Every other note here is an exact quotation.

concepts.name: Wisdom calls out, and the woman named Folly calls out
concepts.why: Name against passages: Proverbs 9:13-18 is Folly's call, not Wisdom's, so the present name says less than the passages hold. The pairing is the text's own (9:3 and 9:15 both 'call out'), so keep the passage and say so in the name rather than let Folly sit under a heading about Wisdom. Wisdom and Folly are not equated by this; no side is taken on who Wisdom is.

note_fixes: Proverbs 8:27–31: replace the note 'I was a skilled craftsman at His side' with the exact quotation 'I was there when He established the heavens' (v27). 'Skilled craftsman' renders a Hebrew word (amon) whose meaning is disputed (craftsman, nursling, constant), so the note rests on one translation's reading; v27 says the same concept without that dispute.
concepts.why: Original arbitrates / Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, biblical-theological readers: Proverbs 8:22-23 'The LORD created me as His first course' says Wisdom's origin, not that the LORD founded the earth by wisdom, so it does not hold this name. It also rests on the BSB's 'created' for Hebrew qanah, which the Vulgate renders 'possessed' and which the Hebrew itself leaves open (compare 'brought forth' in 8:24-25). This is exactly where readers part (whether Wisdom is a creature, and whether Wisdom is the Word), so the site should not display it under a creation-by-wisdom name. The creation-by-wisdom concept is fully carried by Prov 3:19-20, Ps 104:24, Jer 10:12, Job 28:25-27 and Prov 8:27-31. Keep no sub-theme that says Wisdom is or is not the Word: the outline is right that nothing here ties Proverbs 8 to Christ; concept 28 must keep it that way.

Passages hold the concept: Isaiah 55:8-9 (about the LORD's thoughts and ways, said of forgiveness in 55:7) and Deuteronomy 29:29 (secret things and revealed things, with the law) do not speak of wisdom or understanding and merely sit near the idea; secular scholar and Jewish readers of the Hebrew would not find 'where is wisdom' in them. Job 11:7-8 is Zophar, whom the LORD says (42:7) did not speak about Him accurately; the concept stands on Job 28, Eccl 7:23-24, 8:16-17 and Rom 11:33-34 without a friend's speech. Add Job 28:15-18 (moved from concept 3): it is part of the answer 'not with gold, not in the sea'.

Passages hold the concept: Psalm 1:2 says delight in the Law and meditation, nothing about making wise or informing the simple; it is fully at home in concept 9 (where it already sits in Ps 1:1-3). The rest (Ps 19:7-11, Ps 119:98-100, 119:130, Deut 4:6, Prov 6:20-23) say the law/commandment makes wise, gives light, or shows wisdom.

Passages hold the concept: Proverbs 15:11 says Sheol lies open before the LORD and how much more the hearts of men, i.e. that He sees the heart; it says nothing about guarding or about what flows from it. It shares only the word 'heart'.

Passages hold the concept: Proverbs 13:24 is a father's rod and does not say the LORD disciplines; displayed here it puts a contested practice (corporal discipline) under a heading about God's discipline, and a Baptist/Pentecostal and a secular reader would each take it differently. Job 5:17-18 is Eliphaz, of whom the LORD says in 42:7 that he did not speak about Him accurately (concept 18 uses Eliphaz as the example of that); the concept is fully carried by Prov 3:11-12, Ps 94:12, Heb 12:5-6 and 12:11, Rev 3:19.

note_fixes: Order within the concept: place Job 2:3 before Job 2:10 so the passages follow the book.
concepts.why: The original arbitrates (secular scholar, Jewish readers of the Hebrew): Job 13:15 is a textual crux. The consonantal Hebrew (ketiv) reads 'I will not hope', and the reading tradition (qere) reads 'I will hope in Him'; the BSB follows one and the note 'Though He slay me, I will hope in Him' rests on that single choice. The concept does not need it: Job 1:21-22, 2:10, 2:3, Eccl 5:15, 7:14 and 1 Tim 6:7 hold it.

Name against passages: Job 2:11-13 says the three friends came to sympathize and comfort, wept, and sat in silence seven days. It does not say or show them 'miserable comforters'; it is the one passage where the friends do well, and the name says more than it. The concept is fully carried by Job 16:2, 13:4-5, 15:2, 21:34, 4:7-8, 32:2-3 and the LORD's verdict in 42:7-8.

Same consistency as concepts 6 and 14: Job 8:9 is Bildad, one of the friends of whom 42:7 says they did not speak accurately about the LORD. The same figure is carried in Job's own words (7:7, 14:1-2), Ps 144:4, Ps 39:5, Ps 103:14 and Gen 3:19.

Name against passages: the name says 'All flesh'. Psalm 37:2 says only that the evildoers ('they') wither like grass, which is a statement about the wicked, not about all flesh; it already has its place in concept 9 (Ps 37:9-11). The rest (Isa 40:6-8, Ps 103:15-16, Ps 90:5-6, James 1:10-11, 1 Pet 1:24-25) say man or all flesh.

Name against passages, and the point where readers part (all nine, but above all Lutheran, Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox against a secular or Jewish reader): the name says Christ IS the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24, 1:30; Col 2:3 'in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom'). 1 Cor 2:7 speaks of 'the hidden wisdom of God' the apostles speak, and does not say it is Christ; Luke 2:40 and 2:52 say the child was filled with wisdom and grew in wisdom, which is a different claim (the human growth of Jesus, which traditions read through two natures differently) and sets it under a name that asserts a divine identity; Matthew 12:42 says only that One greater than Solomon is here. None of the four holds the concept, and each makes a reader supply the connection. Keep the three that do: 1 Cor 1:24, 1 Cor 1:30, Col 2:2-3. Also confirmed as required: no Old Testament passage (Proverbs 8 or any other) is placed under this concept, and none of its passages is joined to concept 5 by name, so the outline does not say Wisdom is the Word. Note: Messiah/Christology in the links must read as arising from this concept's New Testament passages only (see links).

note_fixes: Job 19:25–27: trim to Job 19:25 (note 'I know that my Redeemer lives' stays exact). Verse 26 'yet in my flesh I will see God' rests on one rendering of Hebrew min-besari, which can be read 'in' or 'apart from' my flesh; the original does not settle it, and Jewish readers, a secular scholar and Christians who read resurrection into it differ. Verse 25 alone holds the hope.
concepts.why: Last-concept check, done as ruled: it is the theme's own words of hope and from within the theme (Prov 23:18, 24:14 in the wise-sayings; Job 19:25, 42:10-12; Ps 42:11, 30:5, 126:5; Lam 3:21-24 is the one passage outside the four books, in the same poetic voice, with the LORD named in its own words). Nothing dark was left out to make room: Job's and Ecclesiastes' hard words keep their own places (16 Why do the wicked prosper, 20 How long O LORD, 21 Futility of futilities, 22 Man is like a breath, 25 time and chance, 17 the LORD gave and has taken away). Prov 24:14 note is exact. Only change is the trim to Job 19:25.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'Wisdom → a tree of life': Proverbs 15:4 says 'A soothing tongue is a tree of life' and does not mention wisdom; under a line headed Wisdom it makes the tongue the same as wisdom. Keep Proverbs 3:18, drop 15:4 from this line (15:4 is already in concept 12) or rename the line 'a tree of life'.

Links: 'Messiah/Christology' is acceptable only as arising from concept 28 (New Testament passages). On a page whose subtitle names Job, Psalms, Proverbs and Ecclesiastes it can otherwise read as 'Old Testament wisdom points to Christ', which no passage here says and which dispensational, Jewish and secular readers would each object to, and which would join Proverbs 8 to Christ by the side door. If the page cannot show which concept the link comes from, drop it.
Links 'Image of God' (James 3:9) and 'Children of God' (Heb 12:5) rest on single New Testament verses; keep, but nothing is claimed beyond the verse.

Eccl 9:4 ('anyone who is joined with the living has hope') and Job 14:7 ('there is hope for a tree') are the same books' own words of hope; optionally add to concept 30 so hope is not carried only by the Psalms, Proverbs and Job's restoration. Not required.
Concept order: 27 then 28 reads on from 1 Cor 1:19-25 into 1 Cor 1:24, which is right, and 29-30 follow so the sequence does not end on Christ. Keep 28 before 29, 30 (not last) for that reason.

missing.sub_theme: Go to the ant, you sluggard
missing.why: The diligent and the sluggard are developed across Proverbs (6, 10, 12, 13, 24, 26), and no concept here carries it; a reader of the wisdom books expects it.

missing.sub_theme: My son, listen to your father's instruction
missing.why: The form of Proverbs 1-9 is a father speaking to a son and Proverbs 31 a mother to a king; teaching handed down in the household is plainly developed and absent. Taken without Proverbs 13:24.
Proverbs 2, 5, 6 and 7 warn at length against the adulteress, and the warning is what the Wisdom/Folly speeches of chapters 8-9 answer; the outline has Folly's call but not the warning it sits among.

missing.sub_theme: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker
missing.why: The poor and the rich, and the LORD as maker of both, are a plain strand in Proverbs and in Job 29-31; none of it appears.

Wisdom and rulers: justice and the king's throne are developed in Proverbs, and 1 Kings 3 is already cited under concept 2 for another point. Take only the verses that name the king and justice, not Proverbs 8:22-31.
